story: At 10:17 on this sunny Friday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is focused on finishing the light strings and wiring the speaker to his golf cart battery at home. Donna is eager and on her way to Magnolia Loop, while Hal, equally focused, is counting and logging the flamingos visible from the street. Meanwhile, Rosa is optimistic in her kitchen, checking the marinade and starting the sides and dessert for tonight's dinner.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Finish securing the light strings and connect the speaker wiring to the battery
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and log the number
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Check the marinade, then get the sides and dessert started for tonight's dinner

gary.thought_process: I've been at the cart for two ticks now, mounting the light strings and running the speaker wiring. Nobody's around, the workbench and cart are right here, and it's a sunny Friday morning with the parade project well underway. Best thing is to keep at it and finish the wiring so I can test the sound system. The 10 PM cutoff is already on file, so I just need to keep the build tidy and plan to test it during daytime hours. Friday dinner with Donna and Rosa is tonight, so I'd like to wrap the wiring by afternoon and still have time to make that cornbread.

parameters.content: Finish securing the light strings and connect the speaker wiring to the battery

donna.thought_process: It's 10:17 on Friday, and Gary's court time was supposed to be at ten. I've confirmed it, packed the bag with the spare paddle and balls, and penciled in dinner at Rosa's at six. Nothing left to check on the calendar, and no one is nearby. Standing around in my living room won't get Gary onto the court or move me up the ladder. I should grab the bag and head out via Magnolia Loop to meet him, and the deviled eggs can wait until this afternoon. Pickleball first.

parameters.content: Heading out to the courts with the paddle bag to meet Gary for his first practice

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with binoculars already used last tick. Nobody's around, and the flamingo flock is right here as an interactive object. Time to do my job properly: count the ornaments visible from the street so I have an exact figure for the architectural review committee under L-02. Facts, not guesses. Friday dinner at Rosa's is tonight, so I'll be fair about it and note the real count, whatever it is.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and log the number

rosa.thought_process: The table is set for four and the main dish is marinating, so the biggest prep is done. It's 10 AM Friday and dinner is tonight. The pantry is the next thing to check: I want to make sure I have sides, drinks, and dessert covered so I'm not scrambling at the last minute. Nobody's nearby, so I'll use the time to work the kitchen and pick up the shift schedule afterward to make sure no per-diem shift crashes into tonight.

parameters.content: Check the marinade, then get the sides and dessert started for tonight's dinner

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
